1

Your Roadmap at a Glance

The plan for your home on one screen

The top of your Roadmap carries the two numbers that matter most: the recommended Coming Soon price and the expected sale price range.

Under them sit the authenticated range from Customary to Premium Value, the money at risk if the home is mispriced or under-prepared, and how the local market is behaving right now.

Pricing is preliminary until a trained Realtor has walked the home. Final values depend on condition, upgrades and any lot premium or discount.

2

Appraisal-Quality Comparable Analysis

The sales an appraiser would use

Your home sits at the top of the table, with the average of the comparable sales right under it.

Each comparable is a real closed sale of similar size, age, location and time, with its assessment, sale price, adjusted price per square foot and sale-to-assessment ratio.

These are the same tests an appraiser applies, so the price holds up when the buyer’s lender orders the appraisal.

3

Price Authenticated by the CST Pricing Team

The ten-cylinder pricing engine

Every value is checked by hand. Cylinders 1–6 run on every home: age and size, price range, price per square foot, assessment, market anomalies and inflation.

Cylinders 7–10 fire only when they apply: neighborhood, a premium or discount carried from the purchase, extraordinary improvements, and detriments.

Two filters then turn value into price. The Market Condition Filter sets the strategy for today’s market, and the Threshold Filter places the price just under a buyer search band so the home appears in every search for that range.

4

Your Values and What You Walk Away With

Dated, Customary and Premium, then your net proceeds

The three cards show what the home is worth by condition: Dated, Customary and Premium. Historically, CST listings sell between Customary and Premium Values. Sometimes more.

When the home sells, the SOLD stamp shows where the price landed. This one sold for $2,300,000, 6.4% over Customary Value.

Estimated Seller Net Proceeds starts at the Customary Price. When a contract comes in, type the contract price and it recalculates commission, Grantor’s Tax and fees.

5

Moving the Needle™

What raises the price, and what lowers it

Strategic improvements return about seven times what they cost. Buyers do not pay top dollar for dated or DIY homes.

Moving the Needle Up lists the presentation and buyer-confidence steps that add value: paint, lighting, flooring, landscaping, a pre-listing inspection, full disclosures and premium photography.

Moving the Needle Down shows what buyers discount for, with typical amounts, so you can fix what is fixable before the home goes live.

6

Current Competition

Who you are up against, and how the market is moving

The market reading tells you who is in control. Here, 28% of listings are under contract, a buyer’s market, but 75% of homes listed in the last 30 days went under contract.

Market Strength scores the share under contract and the days on market from 0 to 10. Market Momentum shows which way it is heading.

The Market Update spells out exactly how many competing homes are active, contingent and pending, and whether any have cut their price.

7

CST Pricing Strategy

Where the price goes, and why

The strategy follows the market. In a buyer’s market it is conservative: the price goes to the first buyer threshold under the authenticated value instead of testing above it.

Here the Customary Value of $2,161,027 sits just over the $2,150,000 search band, so the home is placed at $2,149,999 and shows up for every buyer searching that range.

Print the one-page Pricing Strategy Summary to keep the whole plan in hand.

8

Preview

The home goes public before it goes live

Within two days of a signed Listing Agreement, the home is posted on Preview with photographs, descriptions and property information on Zillow, Homes.com, Samson Properties and more.

Buyers learn the home is coming before it can be shown, and the estimated value they see is the same price the home goes live at.

9

Coming Soon

Full marketing, before the first showing

The home is placed on the MLS with full photography, descriptions and marketing.

The Coming Soon price tests the first threshold under Customary Value, the price most likely to draw a first-week buyer.

10

Predictive Analysis Sets the Price

The first week decides the next move

Showings tell us whether the price is reaching buyers. Five or more: hold the price and let the week finish. Fewer than five: move to the next buyer pool.

Pulling the Rip Cord, zero showings, means traffic has stalled and a further step is due. Every price is set in advance, so there are no surprises.

Traffic without an offer is a condition question, not a price one. That is when Moving the Needle is the cheaper fix.
